name: Palau
summary: A yellow disc on a light blue field, set slightly toward the hoist. The disc represents the full moon, which in Palauan tradition marks the best time for fishing, planting and celebrations.
origin: Palau left the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands and became self-governing on 1 January 1981, adopting the flag designed by Blau Skebong. It kept the flag at full independence in 1994.

colors.name: Light blue
colors.meaning: The Pacific Ocean, and the transition from foreign rule to self-government.

symbols.name: Full moon
symbols.description: A yellow disc slightly toward the hoist.
symbols.meaning: The full moon, regarded as the most auspicious time for activities; also peace, love and tranquillity.

facts: Its off-centre disc resembles Japan's and Bangladesh's flags.
Palau was under Japanese rule from 1914 to 1944.
The moon is placed off-centre so it appears centred when the flag flies.
clues: A yellow disc set slightly toward the hoist on light blue.
Its disc is the full moon, a good time for fishing and planting.
It looks like an Asian sun flag recoloured.
